Detecting and Removing Malware

Moved topic Removal of Malware from BEC Products to chapter Peripherals and reworded topic heading.

Added Important note if malware is suspected on an instrument, it should be re-imaged, because this is the only way to be certain any malware present has been removed. If there is data on the instrument that should be preserved, save this data before re-imaging, and restore the data when complete.

Added note if a customer would like information about whether there was any malware on the device, use the following procedures to detect and remove it for them, but inform them we can only guarantee malware removal if we go through the re-imaging procedure.

Added Important note, as part of this procedure, to delete any detection tools copied to the product's hard drive.

Replaced Malware Scan and Removal Process graphic with new graphic labeled Malware Detection and Removal Process.

Reworded for conciseness and corrected grammar, spelling, and formatting.

Detecting and Removing Malware from the Instrument

Added Important note if malware is suspected on an instrument, it should be re-imaged, because this is the only way to be certain any malware present has been removed. If there is data on the instrument that should be preserved, save this data before re-imaging, and restore the data when complete.

Topic Title Description of Change
Preinstallation Information Added updated file with filename DxI 9000 Site Survey.docx, which includes a formatting revision to the note on page 3, additional information about the depth in the space requirements for the DxI 9000 system on page 4, additional information in a note on page 11 that to determine if the instrument can navigate around a corner. Measure the hallway the instrument is in and the diameter of the hallway turning into. Add the two dimensions together and if the value is <102 inches (258 cm). The instrument will not be able to turn the corner. Also, the omission of water requirement details on page 11 and page 12.
Removing Shrink Wrap, Foam, and Cable Ties

Added Important note at the beginning of the Step 2: Remove Cable ties subtopic, that during this procedure, after you remove cable ties for the pipettor and pick-and-place gantries, manually move the gantries to be sure harnesses have been routed properly and so that there are no movement errors. Observe the spacing between pipettors 2 and 3 over their full range of motion, and pay specific attention to when they are both in the far rear position at the lowest pipetting position. While they are in that position, be sure they do not touch, to eliminate movement errors while running the stress test. Added reworded version of note to steps 19 and 41 of the subtopic.

Installing the DxI 9000 Instrument

Reworded and reformatted text for conciseness by replacing steps for configuring sales and service contact information with cross-reference to Configuring Sales and Service Contact Information, which includes the exact same steps.

Reworded and reformatted text for conciseness by replacing steps for adjusting the system date and time with a cross-reference to Adjusting the System Date and Time, which includes the exact same steps.

Added information in note in step 3 for subtopic Step 12: Initialize and Set Up the Instrument to observe the operation of the instrument. After a system has been shut down for an extended period of time, initialization may fail on the first attempt. Repeat initialization, as necessary. If initialization failures persist, you may need to check or adjust some alignments, camera calibrations, and pressure sensor calibrations. Review system events and troubleshoot messages accordingly. The need to adjust alignments and calibrate cameras and pressure sensors is fully expected and is not something that needs to be reported as an issue.

Added information in Step 19: Calibrate RSM Gripper Timing and Prime the Instrument about first priming an empty substrate system and then priming the instrument. The information was copied from 26.1 Verification of Instrument Installation.

Added information in note for subtopic Step 21: Stress Test the System to observe the operation of the instrument and troubleshoot issues. You may need to check or adjust some alignments, camera calibrations, and pressure sensor calibrations. Review system events and troubleshoot messages accordingly. The need to adjust alignments and calibrate cameras and pressure sensors is fully expected and is not something that needs to be reported as an issue.
